concepts.def: The tendency for theory or research to misrepresent one gender, through alpha bias (exaggerating differences) or beta bias (ignoring them).
The tendency to interpret behaviour through the assumptions of one culture, including ethnocentrism and the imposed etic of applying one culture's measures elsewhere.
The debate over whether behaviour is freely chosen or caused by factors beyond our control, such as biology, environment or the unconscious.
The debate over the relative contributions of inherited, biological factors and environmental experience to the development of behaviour.
The debate between explaining behaviour as an integrated whole and breaking it into simpler component parts such as biological mechanisms.
The contrast between studying individuals in depth (idiographic) and seeking general laws of behaviour across people (nomothetic).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Issues and Debates in Psychology — a core area of A-Level Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Issues and Debates in Psychology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Issues and Debates in Psychology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Exaggerating the differences between men and women is an example of:
options: Alpha bias
Beta bias
An imposed etic
Determinism

mcqs.q: Judging other cultures by the standards of one's own is known as:
options: Ethnocentrism
Reductionism
Free will
The nomothetic approach

mcqs.q: The view that all behaviour is caused by factors beyond our control is called:
options: Determinism
Free will
Holism
The idiographic approach

mcqs.q: Studying a single individual in rich, detailed depth is characteristic of the:
options: Idiographic approach
Nomothetic approach
Biological reductionism
Beta bias

mcqs.q: What is the difference between alpha bias and beta bias?
options: Alpha bias exaggerates differences between genders; beta bias minimises or ignores them.
They both mean treating men and women exactly the same.
Alpha bias is about age and beta bias about culture.
Determinism means everyone behaves identically.

mcqs.q: Does determinism mean behaviour can never be predicted or changed?
options: Determinism means everyone behaves identically.
No; determinism says behaviour has causes, which actually allows it to be predicted and influenced.
Determinism means behaviour is random and unknowable.
Alpha bias is about age and beta bias about culture.

mcqs.q: Is reductionism always a weakness in psychology?
options: No; reducing behaviour to simpler parts can give precise, testable explanations, though it may oversimplify.
Reductionism means studying only large groups.
Reductionism is always bad and never useful.
Alpha bias is about age and beta bias about culture.
